memos.headline: S08 Leads at 52-Week Highs but RSI Warns; S09 and S01 in Relative-Strength Downtrends
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe today. S08 is the standout leader—sitting just 0.1% off its 52-week high with +9.7% 4-week relative strength vs SPY—but its RSI at 78.8 and +13.4% extension above the 50-day mean make me cautious about chasing here; I'd want a pullback toward the 50-day (~275) before adding. S03 and S02 have strong 12-week trends (+24.8% and +30.3% respectively) with healthy RSIs in the mid-to-upper 50s, making them the cleanest intermediate-term longs in the group. On the other side, S09 (RSI 38.6, -6.2% below 50d, -11.1% 4-week relative strength) and S01 (RSI 47.6, -4.1% below 200d, -19.7% 12-week relative strength) are clearly broken relative to the market and I'd avoid both until they reclaim their 50-day averages. S06 is similarly weak with negative returns across all timeframes and -10.4% 12-week relative strength vs SPY.

views.note: Trend is powerful (+18.9% in 12w, near 52w high) but RSI 78.8 and +13.4% above 50d mean signal overextension; would turn long on a pullback to ~290.
Strong 12w trend +24.8%, only -1.6% from highs, RSI 59.7 is healthy, and 12w relative strength vs SPY +14.4%; would reassess below 250.
Best 12w return in the universe at +30.3%, +19.8% relative strength vs SPY over 12w, RSI 57.8 not yet overbought; risk level is the 50d mean area (~338).
Sharp 1w bounce of +7.4% and RSI 69.6 suggest mean-reversion rally within a still-negative 26w trend (-7.6%); still 16.9% off highs so wait for confirmation above 200d mean.
RSI 38.6, -6.5% last week, -15.3% drawdown, and worst 4w relative strength in the universe at -11.1% vs SPY—clear downtrend; would reconsider above 155.
Worst 12w relative strength at -19.7% vs SPY, below both 50d and 200d means, -15.5% off highs—persistent underperformance; needs to reclaim 150 to reconsider.
Flat-to-negative across all timeframes, below both moving averages, -10.4% 12w relative strength vs SPY; no reason to own until price reclaims 310.
Massive 26w gain of +29.9% but 4w relative strength -6.4% and +26.8% above 200d mean suggest the trend is pausing; would get interested on a pullback toward 360 or renewed relative strength.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Show Extraordinary Earnings Power; S09 Earnings Collapse Warrants Caution
memos.body: I see a stark bifurcation in this universe between companies with durable, expanding margins and those facing cash-flow compression. S10 stands out with 85.2% YoY revenue growth, a 71.5% net margin, and net income up 210.6% YoY on just $8.47B of total debt — this is the cleanest earnings profile in the group. S05 is similarly compelling at 56.9% net margin, 21.8% revenue growth, and 81.2% net income growth with minimal leverage ($14.79B debt). On the other end, S09 posted a 45.8% YoY decline in net income on only 2.4% revenue growth, compressing net margin to 4.9% — a clear sign of operating deleverage that I cannot look past. S02 is similarly sluggish at 2.0% revenue growth and flat net income with $77.92B in debt, offering no margin of safety. I would need to see margin stabilization or a return to earnings growth in S09 and S02 before reconsidering.

views.note: 85% revenue growth, 71.5% net margin, 210% net income growth, and near-zero leverage make this the strongest fundamental profile in the universe.
56.9% net margin with 81% net income growth and only $14.79B debt reflects exceptional and durable earnings power.
38.3% net margin, 23.1% net income growth, and moderate $40.26B debt support a high-quality compounder thesis.
76.7% net income growth is impressive but 16.7% net margin and $122.63B in total debt leave less room for error if revenue decelerates.
Solid 16.6% revenue growth and 26.6% margin, but $82.70B debt load tempers enthusiasm; would turn more positive if leverage declines.
22.2% revenue growth and 27.2% net income growth are healthy, but 14.6% net margin and $36.21B debt relative to $17.4B revenue signal high leverage.
33.1% net margin is respectable but $448.76B total debt dwarfs revenue; earnings growth of 12.6% is the slowest among profitable names.
18.5% net margin and 7.4% revenue growth are steady but unexciting; $23.85B debt on $21.23B quarterly revenue is manageable but not compelling.
Net income collapsed 45.8% YoY to a 4.9% margin on anemic 2.4% revenue growth — classic cash-flow compression I refuse to pay for.
2.0% revenue growth, flat net income, 5.6% net margin, and $77.92B debt offer no earnings momentum and thin margin of safety.

memos.headline: Fed on Pause at 3.75% but Sticky 3.8% YoY CPI and Rising Long Rates Argue Against Duration and Favor Defensive Positioning
memos.body: I see a clear pause regime: the fed funds upper bound has been flat at 3.75% for three months after 75 bps of cuts over the past year, while CPI is running at 3.8% YoY—well above target—making further easing unlikely near-term. The 10-year yield has jumped 48 bps over three months to 4.45%, compressing the 10y-2y spread to just 46 bps, which signals the market is repricing for higher-for-longer rates and possibly a growth slowdown. Unemployment at 4.3% is stable but has crept up 10 bps YoY, consistent with a late-cycle deceleration rather than outright recession. This backdrop is negative for duration-sensitive growth and constructive for banks (positive curve, stable credit) and staples (defensive in a slowdown). A CPI print falling below 3.0% or unemployment spiking above 4.6% would shift my regime call toward imminent easing.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth names face headwinds from the 48 bps rise in 10y yields and a Fed unlikely to cut with CPI at 3.8%.
Banks benefit from a positively sloped curve (46 bps 10y-2y), stable unemployment, and a pause regime that keeps net interest margins healthy.
Staples offer defensive positioning as the macro mix of sticky inflation and rising unemployment points to late-cycle deceleration.
Cyclicals face mixed signals—stable labor market supports demand but rising long rates and sticky inflation cap upside.
Energy is a wildcard; inflation staying elevated could reflect commodity strength, but a growth slowdown would weigh on demand.
Long-duration growth is most vulnerable to the 10y yield surge; I would need to see yields retreat below 4.0% to reconsider.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Split: S05 and S07 Momentum Stands Out While S04 and S10 Flash Caution
memos.body: I am reading the earnings-season price reactions as the clearest sentiment signal across this universe. S05 (+10.0%) and S07 (+9.9%) posted the strongest one-day moves on their Q results, suggesting a decisive positive narrative shift that, four weeks later, may still have room to run given continued 'Other Events' filings that keep the news flow alive. On the negative side, S04 saw a -3.9% reaction to its results followed by a management change filing on 5/14, a combination that typically signals deteriorating internal sentiment. S10 is similarly concerning with two separate Departure/Appointment filings in late April and early May preceding a -1.8% earnings reaction on 5/20, pointing to organizational instability that the market is beginning to price. I have moderate conviction on the positive names and lower conviction on the negatives given the limited granularity of the tone data available.

views.note: Strongest earnings-day reaction at +10.0% with two subsequent Other Events filings keeping positive narrative momentum alive.
Near-double-digit +9.9% earnings pop signals a sharp positive tone shift; pre-earnings Other Events filing may have seeded the narrative.
Solid +7.0% earnings reaction followed by a Reg FD disclosure suggests management is actively reinforcing the positive story.
Modest +3.2% earnings reaction is constructive but a preceding director change adds uncertainty; tone is mildly positive but not decisive.
Tepid +1.7% earnings move with multiple Reg FD filings suggests management is managing expectations rather than driving enthusiasm.
Flat -0.8% earnings reaction and heavy governance-related filing volume (bylaws, rights modifications) create noise without a clear directional tone shift.
Negative -3.9% earnings reaction compounded by a subsequent officer departure filing signals deteriorating sentiment.
Two director/officer change filings preceding a -1.8% earnings miss suggest organizational instability the market is starting to discount.
Mild -1.0% earnings reaction plus an immediate officer departure filing hint at negative internal tone; not severe but not encouraging.
Muted +0.8% earnings reaction and routine shareholder vote filing suggest the market has already priced the story; no clear tone inflection.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Still Elevated Despite Easing VIX; Oil at $93 Signals Persistent Energy-Supply Risk
memos.body: I see a bifurcated geopolitical picture as of today. The economic policy uncertainty index sits at 279.84, down 28% over the past month but still up 87% over three months—suggesting a structural shift in the policy regime rather than a one-off shock. VIX at 15.74 and HY OAS at 2.72% indicate credit markets are shrugging off the residual uncertainty, but WTI crude at $92.65 (+38% over three months) tells me energy-supply risk is real and unresolved, likely tied to sanctions enforcement or OPEC+ supply constraints. The flurry of 8-K filings across S06 (four filings in six weeks), S05, S03, S01, and S09 points to companies actively managing disclosure around policy-sensitive developments, though without content detail I cannot confirm whether these relate to export controls, China exposure, or sanctions compliance. My conviction is highest on names with heavy energy exposure or supply-chain concentration risk, and lowest where I lack visibility into the substance of the Reg FD disclosures.

views.note: Four 8-K filings in six weeks suggest active policy-related disclosure; elevated uncertainty warrants caution until content is clarified, but credit markets are calm.
Two 8-K filings in May (8.01 Other Events) could reflect supply-chain or regulatory developments; insufficient detail to take a directional view.
Back-to-back Reg FD disclosures in early April coincided with the peak in policy uncertainty (+87% 3m); energy cost headwinds at $93 WTI add risk if S03 has commodity exposure.
Two Reg FD filings a month apart suggest ongoing investor communication around policy-sensitive topics; VIX decline is supportive but 3m uncertainty surge keeps me sidelined.
April Reg FD disclosures align with the policy-uncertainty spike; no evidence of direct sanctions or export-control exposure, so I stay neutral pending clarity.
8-K filings appear routine; falling VIX and tightening HY spreads suggest the market is comfortable with S07's risk profile amid easing near-term policy fears.
